title: Instance isolation: no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets
description: The agreed principle is that each club owns its instance outright and the original author can never get into it. Three things currently break that. (1) migrations/004 inserts eight named admin accounts with a shared password hash into every new database - remove the INSERTs from the migration file (existing installs have already applied it and are unaffected; their accounts are left alone). (2) Secrets must be generated per instance, never defaulted or shared: the Club Wrapped access code, and later the CourtHive JWT secret (WI-144), are generated on first run and stored on the instance. (3) The app must not send anything to the author: confirm there is no telemetry, update ping or remote logging, and write down every outbound connection the instance makes. Add a startup self-check that refuses to run in production mode with a known default secret.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: The isolation guarantee is the programme's central trust promise; needs a thorough, sceptical pass rather than a mechanical one.

acceptance_criteria: A database created from scratch contains zero user rows until setup creates the first administrator
Real people's names no longer appear in migration 004; the e2e seed provides its own test administrator
No secret has a hardcoded default; anything required is generated with crypto/rand at first run and stored locally

The app starts no outbound connection except those listed in a new 'What this instance connects to' doc section (BHPLTA, open-meteo weather, browser push services, and the container registry for updates)
No analytics, error reporting, licence check or update ping exists, and a test asserts the absence of unexpected hosts in the code
Existing installs upgrade without losing or changing any account

notes: Editing an applied migration is safe here only because golang-migrate tracks version numbers, not checksums. Say so in migrations/README.md, and fix that README's stale 'next available' line.
The author's names remain in git history; that is accepted.
Hardcoded jim.tennis values (VAPID subscriber in internal/webpush/webpush.go:273, iCal UID domain in internal/services/ical_generator.go:38) are replaced by the instance's public URL in WI-126.

testing_requirements: Fresh-database test asserting an empty users table after migrations
Upgrade test: apply to a copy of a populated database and assert accounts unchanged

context.user_story: As a club, I want certainty that nobody outside my club - including the software's author - has an account or a key to my instance.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
